how_to_use: The brief asks for a section where suggestions can be reviewed and a path chosen before anything is implemented, and for suggestions that discover missing information rather than restate it. Each row below has a pre-condition (what must be true before it is worth doing), a cost, the decision it changes, and the evidence it would produce. Nothing on this page has been implemented by this session unless the 'done' column says so.

rows.title: Capture the official inactive list 90 minutes before every kickoff
rows.what: Store the 46-man inactive list per game, with the fetch timestamp and a raw hash, in an append-only store. This is the single cheapest data addition available and it is the only way to turn 'a backup probably started' into 'a backup played'.
rows.why: Without it the availability graph (the brief's first-class dataset) has no 'who actually played' half, and no injury designation can ever be calibrated.
rows.precondition: an official nfl.com or club page that publishes the list in a parseable form; this must be checked, not assumed
rows.cost: one scheduled capture per game window, about 3 windows per week
rows.produces: play/no-play per listed player per week, which is the denominator for Q06
rows.changes_decision: Q06, Q15, and whether a designation becomes a feature
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: at least one full season of designations joined to inactives, with a play rate and Wilson interval per designation

rows.title: Archive the official Game Book for every played game, and read the starters out of it
rows.what: The Game Book names the actual starters. Archiving it replaces the depth-chart projection with an observation and makes the availability graph auditable.
rows.why: The brief orders this route before snap counts, and the repository is at 0 of 137 played games archived.
rows.precondition: the Game Book is retrievable and its layout is stable enough to parse; a spot check on one game must succeed before a sweep is attempted
rows.cost: one fetch per played game, then a parser that must be pinned to expected fields
rows.produces: actual starters for 137 games immediately, and every future game
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: 137 of 137 played 2026 games archived, with the starter list extracted and compared with the depth chart

rows.title: Widen the injury capture to Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and pre-kickoff, and publish the delta
rows.what: The capture workflow already exists; it runs too rarely. Move it to a schedule that produces at least three distinct days per week and store the difference between readings, not only the snapshot.
rows.why: The brief's 'surprise, not level' requirement is unreachable from 2 capture days. It needs transitions: DNP to LP to FP, Questionable to Out.
rows.cost: four scheduled runs a week; no new code beyond a delta store
rows.produces: a dated series and the designation-change count the readiness gate is waiting for
rows.changes_decision: Q05, and the ablation in Q07
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: 2 or more capture days AND at least 1 recorded designation change (the repository's own gate)
rows.status: suggested — cheapest of all; the gate is one week away

rows.title: Write the price-data policy before the next backtest, and store opening and closing numbers
rows.what: Name the price source, the timestamp rule, the push/void treatment, and the missing-price fallback. Then start a snapshot store that records an opening and a closing observation per market per game, with a hash and a time.
rows.why: The brief asks for closing-line value as a qualifying metric and for the price-data policy to be decided before any backtest is published. Neither is possible from one line per game.
rows.precondition: a named source that publishes both an early and a late number, and a decision that it is acceptable (no official source exists)
rows.cost: two captures per week per originated game, from now on — it cannot be backfilled
rows.produces: closing-line value, line-move history, and a defensible answer to 'what price did you actually get'
rows.changes_decision: Q10, Q11, and whether any backtest may be published at all
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: a recorded policy plus opening-to-closing coverage on every originated game for one full week

rows.title: Collapse the four pre-registration registries into one, keeping every hash
rows.what: Choose one registry as authoritative, import the other three by reference (hash plus rule text location), and keep a single checker. Do not delete any registration record.
rows.why: Four registries with four checkers means 'registered' has four meanings, and the leaderboard gate depends on which one a page reads.
rows.precondition: a named owner; this is a board decision, not a code change
rows.produces: one registration hash per rule, verifiable from git
rows.changes_decision: Q16, and the authority of the ranked leaderboard
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: one checker in CI, and every ranked row carrying a hash that the checker resolves to a commit

rows.title: Publish one alias table for club codes and fail the build on an unmapped code
rows.what: A single table keyed on the official code (AZ, LA) with each feed's alias (ARI, LAR), used by every join, plus a gate that refuses to build when a join sees a code it does not know.
rows.why: A join on the raw code already drops one club in 32, and the repository stores the Cardinals under two different codes in different files.
rows.produces: joins that either work or fail loudly
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: a deliberate test that injects an unknown code and watches the build fail

rows.title: Add a 'definition' cell to every numeric column on a published table
rows.what: One line beside the column header saying exactly what is counted. The depth ladder's 'missing starter' column currently means two things at once (pressed-into-duty and empty slot), and only a definition prevents a 38-slot misreading.
rows.why: A correct number with an ambiguous label is how honest tables get misread.
rows.produces: tables a reader can act on without reading the generator
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: every numeric column on the site resolves to a definition string
rows.status: partly done — this sub-site prints the definition on every column it publishes; the older pages do not

rows.title: Make the fixture-context table the only way a model sees a schedule fact
rows.what: The Week 11 context table (weekday, kickoff, rest days, short week, division game, venue, neutral site) already exists and its 13 rows were independently confirmed this session against the official pages. Point every model at that table instead of at per-model ad-hoc joins.
rows.why: One table, one verification, one place to see a wrong fact. The brief asks for a fixture-context feature set built only from published facts; that is this table, and it is already built.
rows.precondition: the two remaining unpublished facts (roof and surface) must be either sourced officially or left blank — the feed's values are not official
rows.produces: a single auditable input for schedule context
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: every model that uses rest, bye or venue reads the one table, and the table passes its own official re-check
rows.status: suggested — the table exists; the wiring does not

rows.title: Run the availability ablation on the surprise feature, not on a snapshot
rows.what: The one ablation already run found nothing (+0.0007 points of MAE, interval [-0.0226, +0.0216]) using a snapshot feature. Repeat it on the surprise feature once SG-03 exists, with the identical model and a chronological holdout.
rows.why: The brief forbids a fixed points penalty for a missing starter and asks for a test with uncertainty. That test has been built; it just needs a feature with information in it.
rows.precondition: SG-02 and SG-03 — at least one season of confirmed starters and a dated series
rows.cost: one modelling session per ablations pass
rows.produces: a defensible answer to 'do availability features earn anything'
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: an interval on the difference that excludes zero in the useful direction, on a holdout the feature was not designed on
rows.status: suggested — the null result is already published rather than hidden

rows.title: Keep the leaderboard empty until a rule clears all eight gates, and say so on the front page
rows.what: An empty ranked board is correct, not a failure. Publish the gate matrix, the luck band and the power number beside it, so a reader understands why it is empty rather than assuming the work is unfinished.
rows.why: The brief forbids backtest numbers on the leaderboard and asks for a two-stage qualification. A board that ranks nothing is the honest consequence.
rows.produces: a leaderboard a reader can trust precisely because it is empty
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: a strategy that clears all eight gates on a prospective sample
rows.status: done — this sub-site publishes the empty board with the reason, and quarantines every backtest number in a labelled archive block

rows.title: Reduce the site to one front door and group the rest by category
rows.what: The repository publishes about 194 HTML pages across 13 sub-sites, with a 38-entry header nav and four competing landing pages. Keep them all; give a reader one page that says what each one answers, and stop putting 38 links in the header.
rows.why: A decision-support site whose front door requires a map is not decision support. The brief asks for a clean landing page with subpages organised by category.
rows.cost: one page plus a nav decision (owned by the generators, so this session publishes its own sub-site and logs the request instead of editing other sessions' nav)
rows.produces: a front door with eight categories and a 'what is missing' section
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: one nav entry, under 12 header links, and every page reachable within two clicks of a category
rows.status: done for this sub-site — brief/index.html is that front door; the rest of the site is linked, not changed

rows.title: Print the capture time and the source hash on every row that comes from a live page
rows.what: A snapshot without a clock is not evidence. The injury capture stores a date but not a time; a page that shows it cannot say how old it is.
rows.why: The brief asks for every injury-hub read to be stored with its clock time, and for the delta rather than the level.
rows.precondition: the capture tool must record the clock — the existing heartbeat.jsonl already does, so this is a join, not new capture
rows.produces: every published row can be dated to the hour
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: no published row lacks a capture timestamp
rows.status: partly done — this sub-site prints the capture timestamp on every captured table; the injury TSV's own manifest records a date only (flag CAP-06 upstream)

rows.title: Write down what would make the site wrong, before the season ends
rows.what: Twelve claims already carry a two-sided mind-changer. Extend the same field to the 31 strategy records and to the operational claims (the depth projection, the injury series, the price store).
rows.why: The brief asks for a two-sided field on every strategy entry. A claim without a falsifier is a belief.
rows.produces: a register where every published number has an exit condition
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: one mind-changer per ranked row, enforced by the existing gate

rows.title: Decide the publication terms before the row-level tables spread further
rows.what: Separate the public analysis layer from a private row-level layer, and record the terms review that justifies the split.
rows.why: The brief asks for exactly this separation, and the repository currently publishes row-level injury rows with no recorded terms review.
rows.precondition: a reviewer who reads the terms and records the conclusion with a date
rows.cost: one review, then a publishing rule the build enforces
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: a dated terms record in the repository and a build rule that keeps row-level data out of the public tree unless the record permits it
rows.status: suggested — PR #79 is an open attempt and has not merged

rows.title: Publish a weekly 'what changed' diff next to the snapshot
rows.what: A diff of standings, ratings, availability and designations between two dated captures, with the date of each side printed.
rows.why: This session measured 24 of 32 club records moving in three days. A static snapshot hides that; a diff is the information.
rows.precondition: two dated captures (exists for standings and injuries; missing for ratings)
rows.produces: the direction of travel, not just the position
rows.gate_that_would_confirm: every published snapshot has a diff against its predecessor, or states that it is the first
rows.status: suggested — the shadow/ sub-site has a what-changed page from another session; this session's measurements confirm the need

review_process: A reviewer picks a row, records the choice and the date, and only then is anything implemented. The pre-condition column exists so that a suggestion cannot be started before the evidence it needs is in hand — that is the failure mode this repository has hit repeatedly (a page built before its source was verified, then corrected three times).
